properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by upstream dam release continues.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of the Verde River between Fort McDowell and the

be unsafe.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...

Salt River confluence measured a flow exceeding 1800 cfs.

downstream towards the confluence with the Salt River.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

deaths occur in vehicles.

Flooding is occurring. It is important to know where you are relative
to streams, rivers, or creeks. Campers and hikers should avoid
streams or creeks.

properties.title: Flood Advisory issued November 8 at 8:12AM CST by NWS Brownsville TX
properties.description:
...The National Weather Service in Brownsville has issued a Flood
Advisory for the following rivers in Texas...

Los Olmos Creek Near Falfurrias affecting Brooks County.

.Excessive rainfall is forecast to continue upstream of Los Olmos
into early this week, leading to a rise in river levels that may
approach action stage late tonight.

For the Los Olmos Creek...including Falfurrias...elevated river
levels are forecast.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Los Olmos Creek near Falfurrias.

* WHEN...From this morning until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 7.0 feet, Minor lowland flooding reaches 120 feet wide
into flood plain-persons vulnerable to lowland flooding should move
equipment to higher ground.

At 9.0 feet, Flow is high enough to close FM 1418 as water is
covering the bridge.

At 10.0 feet, Flow escapes from the Los Olmos drainage into the Palo
Blanco drainage area.

At 11.0 feet, Minor flooding with lowland flooding 300 feet wide into
the flood plain.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:15 AM CST Sunday the stage was 1.2 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 5.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 10.7 feet
early Tuesday morning.
- Action stage is 5.0 feet. The river is expected to reach action
stage late tonight.
- Flood stage is 11.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
If you are in the advisory area, remain alert to possible flooding or
the possibility of the advisory being upgraded to a warning.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

Stay tuned to further developments by listening to your local radio,
television, or NOAA Weather Radio for further information.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this evening at 815 PM CST.

Raceway and Arlington.

properties.title: Flash Flood Warning issued November 8 at 7:57AM CST until November 8 at 11:00AM CST by NWS Corpus Christi TX
properties.description:
FFWCRP

The National Weather Service in Corpus Christi has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Southeastern Duval County in south central Texas...
Southwestern Jim Wells County in south central Texas...
Northwestern Kleberg County in south central Texas...

* Until 1100 AM CST.

* At 757 AM CST, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
thunderstorms producing heavy rain across the warned area. Between
2 and 5 inches of rain have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts of
2 to 4 inches are possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is
ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar and automated gauges.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Kingsville, Benavides, Palito Blanco, San Jose, Ben Bolt, Rios and
Cruz Calle.

This includes US Highway 281 between mile markers 678 and 698.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.
